context.objective: Test whether animal meropenem PK and preclinical PK/PD can predict human exposure and support efficacious-dose estimation.

study.regimen: Partial, independent IV/SC regimens and dose-fractionation/humanized-regimen descriptions (SC007, SC009, SC010, SC014, SC020, SC021, SC022).
study.population: Mouse, rat, guinea pig, rabbit, beagle dog, rhesus and cynomolgus monkeys, pregnant monkeys, and later human validation (SC007, SC022, SC023, SC026).
study.system: Animal disposition and infection studies, with in-vitro binding, enzyme and MIC sources (SC007, SC009, SC018, SC019, SC024).
study.measurements: PK, binding, distribution/excretion, MIC and preclinical PD summaries (SC007, SC009, SC016, SC024).
study.methods: Planned animal PK modeling, human translation, Emax/Hill index comparison, independent validation and PTA simulation (SC030, SC032, SC034, SC037, SC038).

items.statement: Meropenem is a known-drug test case with existing human PK intended for independent validation.
The primary outcome is model feasibility, not a clinical dosing recommendation or proof of generalizability.
Meropenem is the sole test drug; imipenem/cilastatin, ertapenem and other source comparators must not substitute for it.

The project follows the translational objective of Sou T et al., Model-Informed Drug Development for Antimicrobials: Translational PK and PK/PD Modeling to Predict an Efficacious Human Dose for Apramycin, Clinical Pharmacology & Therapeutics, 2021;109:1063-1073, https://doi.org/10.1002/cpt.2104.
Do not import the apramycin model or its parameters from SC004.

Meropenem_source_tables_by_species.xlsx is the single animal and in-vitro data workbook; its sheets retain source-shaped tables and notes rather than a ready-made modeling dataset. These are proposal-described resource roles, not findings from inspecting the workbook.

Cross_species describes one study giving 20 mg/kg IV to mouse, rat, guinea pig, rabbit, beagle dog and rhesus monkey. It includes digitized mean plasma curves, PK parameters, urinary recovery, dose effects in mice and guinea pigs, tissue levels, renal DHP-I kinetics and serum binding, plus a second laboratory's plasma-binding table. Guinea pig occurs only on this sheet. Only the stated dosing component is supplied in this proposal description.
Use Cross_species for the core between-species comparison.

Mouse includes PK parameters and fitted dose-fractionation PD parameters for A. baumannii in a neutropenic thigh model; the proposal supplies a dose-fractionation description rather than a numerical schedule. See MI001.
A separate Mouse study compares humanized regimens against ESBL E. coli and K. pneumoniae in renally impaired mice; the proposal describes the regimen type without its numerical schedule.
Mouse also includes population PK with ELF in a P. aeruginosa pneumonia model.
Mouse additionally contains text-only PK and binding information.
Use Mouse sources for PK and eligible PD analysis.

Rat includes plasma levels after single IV dosing and after daily IV dosing for 92 days; some means contain substituted detection-limit values. These are separate dosing descriptions, without numerical dose amounts in the proposal.
Rat separately includes 14C excretion and urinary metabolite profiles.
Rat includes PK, target attainment and survival in neutropenic septic rats sampled as whole blood.
Use Rat sources for systemic PK; survival must not be treated as a bacterial-burden endpoint.

Rabbit includes population PK with plasma and CSF compartments in a P. aeruginosa meningoencephalitis model; concentrations are available only as model parameters. Component eligibility is addressed by SC031 and MI002.
Rabbit also includes in-vitro plasma binding from a preprint.

Dog includes 14C and unlabelled PK at 120 mg/kg IV with the open-ring metabolite H-4295, tissue radioactivity and 14-day repeat dosing. The proposal does not specify the repeat-dose schedule or establish that its doses equal the stated PK dose.
A separate abstract-only Dog study reports IV and SC administration at 20 mg/kg; other dosing components are not stated in the proposal.
Monkey includes 14C PK and excretion at 300 mg/kg IV in cynomolgus monkeys. This is the stated dosing component, subject to MI003.
Monkey separately includes maternal and fetal plasma levels in pregnant monkeys; see MI003.

In_vitro_MIC contains EUCAST MIC distributions by organism from a 2009 snapshot, comparative MICs for the A. baumannii thigh isolates, and single-strain MICs stated in animal studies. See MI012 and MI013.
Use matched strain MICs for PD; a population MIC distribution cannot replace them. Distribution-based attainment is handled separately in SC038.

Human reference tables comprise label PK statements, a healthy-volunteer study, EUCAST summary PK and human rows removed from animal sources. Their availability and release conditions are owned by MI004.
Meropenem_project_proposal.docx defines the task: Animal to Human Translation of Meropenem, Feasibility study, Version 1.0 (draft), 9 October 2026.
AGENT_README.md is described as explaining package use and known gaps; its body has not been inspected in this transformation.

Planned data preparation splits mixed source blocks into PK, PD, MIC and validation inputs; checks provenance, units, dose histories, analytes, matrices, experimental units and missing fields; and identifies usable records and unresolved gaps before fitting.

Planned animal PK work selects eligible systemic models for each species with usable data, evaluates fit and parameter identifiability, evaluates held-out prediction where design permits, and documents exclusion or exploratory use of summary-only, figure-only or radiolabel evidence. Component support is governed by SC031.
Add pulmonary or CSF components only where supported. For the rabbit model-parameter-only concentrations in SC018, assess whether they support a model component or only exploratory constraints.

Planned human translation uses supported animal models with body size, protein binding, renal elimination and justified physiological relationships. Compare scaling with and without each species rather than assuming more species is better.

Predict human concentration-time profiles, AUC, Cmax and fT>MIC with uncertainty under specified doses and infusion durations, then freeze the animal model, scaling and predictions. Access to human outcomes follows MI004; prediction conditions remain subject to MI007.

For eligible data, planned PK/PD analysis compares fT>MIC, fAUC/MIC and fCmax/MIC using ordinary Emax and sigmoid Emax/Hill regression separately by organism and infection site. Estimate supported exposure targets, or report that available data cannot determine a best index or target.

Give all three indices and both regression families in SC034 equal eligibility. Compare them on the same matched response records, strain MICs, free-exposure basis, dosing histories, time windows and likelihood. Register the selection rule before fitting; report R², AIC/BIC, stability and identifiability while counting the extra Hill parameter. Do not select by R² alone or force a winner.
Keep stasis, 1-log and 2-log kill targets separate. A target from one organism, infection site or endpoint—thigh CFU, lung ELF, CSF or survival—cannot set another.

Planned human validation applies the frozen model to the doses and infusion conditions in SC026, compares predicted and observed plasma PK, and assesses other matrices separately when compatible data exist. Report bias, precision, exposure agreement and predictive uncertainty against criteria fixed before validation.

After PK validation and PD qualification, planned PTA simulation uses a prespecified human population and dosing scenarios, including infusion duration, to estimate attainment at each MIC. Process the MIC distribution and report distribution-weighted attainment separately. Include an exploratory efficacious-dose estimate where supported, with uncertainty; deliver PTA tables/curves, a feasibility conclusion and reproducible code. If required inputs are missing, report why PTA is not estimable.

Preserve source identifiers, units, missing values and detection limits. Group means, published fitted parameters and digitized points are not individual animals; flag means containing substituted detection-limit values. Do not invent IDs, variability—including interindividual variability from group summaries—exposure-response links or missing measurements.

Keep routes; unchanged meropenem, H-4295 and total 14C; total versus unbound drug; and plasma, serum, whole blood, ELF, CSF, tissue fluid and tissue homogenate separate. Separate per-animal from per-kilogram parameters and neutropenic, renally impaired, septic, infected, pregnant and repeat-dose animals from healthy single-dose animals. In-vitro DHP-I kinetics are not PK. Every conversion or physiological bridge requires a recorded justification.
Reported bound-fraction alternatives are approximately 10%, 24% and 34% for mouse, and below 1%, 7.5% and 12% for dog. Their unresolved source conflicts are owned by MI005 and MI006.
Never average conflicting within-species binding sources; carry fu as a sensitivity parameter.
Humanized regimens were designed from human PK.

Published PD targets and conclusions must not set primary-analysis starting values, bounds, priors or rankings. Do not use humanized regimens to tune scaling, and do not let human outcomes tune the animal model or scaling. Freeze PD targets before their respective validation or dose-simulation steps; the other freezes are specified in SC033, SC037 and SC046. Preserve the original validation result if a later model is revised.
The EUCAST distributions were compiled to set epidemiological cut-offs.

Preserve MIC bins, units, counts, denominators and censored categories. Do not interpret the EUCAST distributions as resistance rates. Derive probabilities transparently, freeze the MIC distribution/input before its applicable validation or dose-simulation step, and never silently renormalize incomplete coverage.
Propagate parameter, binding, PD-target and MIC uncertainty.
Do not equate a successful fit with predictive validation or human PK agreement with validation of antibacterial efficacy or safety.
Preserve failures and data gaps; save transformations, assumptions, code, seeds and results; obtain human review before fitting.

items.impact: The feasibility of an eligible matched-record PD index comparison cannot be established from the proposal's fitted-parameter descriptions alone.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal explicitly states that no Mouse-sheet source gives per-regimen CFU tables. This is a source-reported limitation; attachment bodies remain NOT_SEARCHED.
items.clarification: Assess what PD analyses the described sources can support, and document whether the missing response tables prevent the comparison in SC034–SC035.

items.impact: Rabbit records cannot yet be assigned a supported component role or an exploratory-only role.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal requires the assessment in SC031 but does not report its outcome; attachments have not been assessed.
items.clarification: Evaluate the support supplied by SC018 and record the resulting eligibility decision under SC031.

items.field: Monkey source animal counts and doses
items.impact: Animal-count interpretation and dose-linked use of Monkey records remain unresolved.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal reports within-source disagreement in animal counts and doses for the Monkey material. It does not reproduce the conflicting alternatives, and attachment bodies are NOT_SEARCHED.
items.clarification: Retain the animal counts and doses as printed, locate their exact study contexts during authorized preparation, and record the unresolved alternatives without silently reconciling them.

items.field: Human validation data availability and release
items.impact: Independent comparison with human observations must await the permitted release.
items.why_it_matters: Human validation data are not in the supplied package. The reference tables described in SC026 are held in a separate file and released only at task 5, after the animal model, scaling and predictions are frozen.
items.clarification: At task 5, release the separate human reference file only after confirming the required freezes; do not access its outcomes earlier.

items.impact: A single resolved mouse binding value cannot be used for free-exposure interpretation or translation.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal identifies conflicting mouse binding sources; the reported alternatives are preserved in SC041.
items.clarification: Retain the source-specific alternatives and assess their applicability under SC042 without averaging them.

items.impact: A single resolved dog binding value cannot be used for free-exposure interpretation or translation.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal identifies conflicting dog binding sources; the reported alternatives are preserved in SC041.
items.clarification: Retain the source-specific alternatives and assess their applicability under SC042 without averaging them.

items.field: Human PK prediction doses and infusion durations
items.impact: The prospective profiles and exposure metrics in SC033 cannot be defined for a concrete prediction setting.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal calls for specified doses and infusion durations but supplies no chosen human prediction values. This is proposal-bounded missingness, not a finding about unread reference files.
items.clarification: Specify the prospective human PK prediction doses and infusion durations before generating and freezing the predictions.

items.impact: Index selection cannot proceed under a registered decision rule.
items.why_it_matters: SC035 requires registration before fitting, but the proposal does not specify the selection rule.
items.clarification: Prespecify and register the index-selection rule while retaining the comparison constraints in SC035.

items.impact: Human prediction performance cannot receive a prespecified acceptance judgment.
items.why_it_matters: SC037 names performance measures but the proposal does not define the criteria against which they will be judged.
items.clarification: Fix the human validation criteria before validation and bind them to the frozen prediction.

items.impact: PTA simulation lacks its prespecified target-population definition.
items.why_it_matters: The population required by SC038 is not specified in the proposal.
items.clarification: Prespecify the human population before PTA simulation, with any variability basis supported or explicitly limited as required by MI014.

items.impact: PTA cannot be calculated for defined regimens or infusion-duration scenarios.
items.why_it_matters: SC038 requires prespecified dosing scenarios including infusion duration, but the proposal gives no scenario choices.
items.clarification: Prespecify the human PTA dosing scenarios and infusion durations before simulation.

items.impact: The denominator basis for deriving MIC probabilities requires explicit resolution.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal explicitly states that the EUCAST distributions carry no totals; this source-reported gap is not an attachment inspection result.
items.clarification: Establish and document a defensible denominator basis from authorized inputs, or retain the resulting limitation on distribution-weighted attainment.

items.field: MIC coverage assessment and probability handling
items.impact: A transparent MIC probability distribution cannot yet be frozen for weighted attainment.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal does not assess coverage or specify treatment of any incomplete coverage. Its prohibition in SC046 does not establish that coverage is actually incomplete.
items.clarification: Assess MIC coverage and record probability handling, preserving censored categories and any unresolved limitation under SC046.

items.impact: A defensible individual-variability basis for subsequent population predictions has not been established.
items.why_it_matters: The proposal describes summary-level evidence and prohibits invented variability, but does not establish whether defensible individual PK variability can be supported. Attachment bodies remain NOT_SEARCHED.
items.clarification: Assess the available experimental units and variability evidence during PK work; record supported variability or the resulting limitation without manufacturing it from group summaries.
